myth: A staffing chart has a direction: teacher numbers in Lunenburg either went up or they went down.
mechanism: Which window a chart uses. The sign of a change is a property of the START and END years, not of the series — so two true charts can point opposite ways.
note: Names nobody. Both charts residents have been shown are real; the card supplies the missing half — ask any staffing chart which year it starts.

myth: A pupil leaving takes their share of state aid with them, so the aid falls with enrolment.
mechanism: How a Chapter 70 increment works. Lunenburg is held at the minimum, so the formula pays a flat per-pupil INCREASE rather than a per-pupil amount — the aid moves by the increment, not by the average.
note: The obvious reading of a per-pupil aid figure, and it is the arithmetic that is misleading rather than anybody saying it.

myth: A published cut list is the list of cuts: those positions are going.
mechanism: What a published cut list IS. It is a stage in an argument — a draft put out for a vote that has not happened — and positions leave it between one printing and the next.
note: Both are true: the list is real and it is not a decision. The card confirms the worry and supplies the stage the document sits at.
